thread:
Alex Rivera: quick RFC follow-up: we need to decide admission interface boundaries for fairness. current problem: abuse score and weight adjustments are too tightly coupled to admit path.
Nora Singh: Yup. Observed tight coupling caused an explosion of callers re-evaluating weights on every retry.
Priya Kapoor: Proposal A: keep AdmitRequest minimal (tenant_id, request_id, tokens_needed) and attach an optional Attribution header that upstreams can set. Abuse scores live in a separate Lookup API.
Dan Miller: Proposal B: enrich AdmitRequest with `priority_hint` and `abuse_score` fields so proxies can short-circuit; avoids extra RPC in the hot path. Tradeoff: couples admission to abuse model schema.
Alex Rivera: Metrics from sandbox: adding abuse_score field saved ~1.8ms p99 in our local proxy microbench but increased complexity in protobufs and rollout surface.
RateBot: synthetic-run fairness-mix-2000: skew observed when abuse_score present and weight normalization applied incorrectly.
Nora Singh: Key concern: schema churn. Abuse models will change weekly during experiments. We can't keep migrating Admit proto.
Priya Kapoor: What about a hybrid: sticky hint field `priority_hint` (enum LOW/MED/HIGH) in AdmitRequest and decouple raw `abuse_score` to a sidecar Lookup service with caching TTL. That gives low-bandwidth fast-path while keeping experiments free to iterate.
Dan Miller: Caching TTL could be 5s by default and configurable per-tenant. But caching opens stale decisions: a client could be temporarily abusive and gain priority for TTL window. Need probation tokens to mitigate.
Alex Rivera: Implementation sketch for proto (minimal):
```proto
message AdmitRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string request_id = 2;
  int32 tokens = 3;
  PriorityHint priority = 4; // LOW, MED, HIGH
}
enum PriorityHint { PH_UNKNOWN = 0; PH_LOW = 1; PH_MED = 2; PH_HIGH = 3; }
```
Priya Kapoor: Sidecar Lookup API: GET /abuse/score?tenant=t-123 -> {score: 0.72, model_version: "v42", as_of: 1711111111}. Cache keyed by tenant + model_version.
Nora Singh: Also require an audit header when proxy sets priority_hint: `X-Priority-Source: cached|lookup|operator`. That helps debug and for replay.
RateBot: canary test queued: admit-hybrid-ttl-5s. Results ETA ~2 hours.
Dan Miller: Rollout plan: 1) deploy proto with PriorityHint default PH_UNKNOWN, 2) implement lookup sidecar behind feature flag, 3) default proxies to call lookup for tenants flagged in experiments, 4) observe p99 latency and fairness metrics.
Priya Kapoor: Safety: if lookup unavailable, AdmitRequest must not fail; fallback behavior: treat unknown as PH_LOW and surface metric `admit_lookup_down` with tenant id.
Alex Rivera: Telemetry: emit admit_request.{priority_hint, resolved_priority, lookup_latency, lookup_cache_hit} plus fairness_exposure per-tenant. Also add a tracing tag `admit.priority.source`.
Nora Singh: Abuse team ask: we want to experiment on continuous scores for a bit. Will accept the sidecar approach as it lets us iterate without proto churn.
Dan Miller: One more boundary: who normalizes weights? Runtime or admission? If normalized in admission, it must be deterministic across replicas. I vote runtime-normalization at serving layer and admission provides base priority.
Priya Kapoor: Agreed. Admission returns admitted: true/false and suggested_priority. Serving applies normalization against per-tenant caps.
Alex Rivera: Decision summary: hybrid interface. Add PriorityHint to AdmitRequest, decouple raw abuse_score to sidecar Lookup with TTL caching, fallback to PH_LOW when lookup down, runtime to perform final weight normalization. Action items: Alex open RFC PR, Priya build sidecar spec, Dan add fallback probe and normalization tests, Nora coordinate experiments with Abuse.
EngInfraBot: created task ENG-3421 (admit-priority-hint-proto) and ENG-3422 (abuse-lookup-sidecar).
Alex Rivera: Thanks all. If nothing else, I'll post the RFC link in this thread when ready. /cc @eng-platform
